title: Physics on arXiv — weekly window ending 2026-11-26
global_caveat: Inferred ranking; arXiv has no official trending chart. Attention signals are sparse and Semantic Scholar citation data was unavailable, so citation evidence for recent papers is limited. Cross-listing and recency should not be mistaken for popularity.

sections.title: An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
sections.abstract: The author constructs a background-independent quantization of four-dimensional vacuum general relativity using intersecting null cones, deriving finite transition amplitudes and black-hole entropy within the proposed framework.
sections.claimed_result: The author derives an absolutely convergent Lorentzian path integral, a finite graviton-pair amplitude, finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces for bounded macroscopic causal diamonds, and Bekenstein–Hawking entropy with a one-loop logarithmic correction.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; canonical reduction and quantization of first-order gravity on intersecting null cones, with amplitude and semiclassical analyses
sections.unique_caveat: Results are within a specific proposed null-boundary quantization and causal-diamond construction; theoretical checks are not empirical validation of a complete quantum-gravity theory.

sections.title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
sections.abstract: The authors introduce a sealed-world benchmark that evaluates whether AI agents can deliver robust high-energy-physics analyses across hidden CMS simulation datasets with injected signals and detector variations.
sections.claimed_result: Across four tasks based on CMS open data, the strongest tested model scored 60% of the expert-reference score on average; the paper proposes sealed injected datasets as a way to test analysis accuracy and robustness.
sections.evidence_type: computational; agent workflows tested on four CMS-simulation benchmark tasks using sealed worlds
sections.unique_caveat: The worlds come from one experiment and mostly vary signal and detector response; results depend on model choices, score weights and expert references, and other generators/experiments remain to be tested.

sections.title: Constraining Planet Nine with Pulsar Timing: Orbit Determination Method from the Acceleration, Jerk, and Snap of the Solar System Barycenter
sections.abstract: The authors show how pulsar timing measurements of solar-system-barycenter acceleration, jerk and snap could constrain a hypothetical Planet Nine's orbit, with jerk and snap needed to remove degeneracies.
sections.claimed_result: The authors derive an orbit-inversion method and show that acceleration and jerk alone leave a one-parameter family, while snap is needed for a unique orbit; their method recovers literature-consistent masses for Uranus and Neptune.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical/computational; analytic orbit determination applied to pulsar spin-frequency and binary-orbital-period derivatives
sections.unique_caveat: This is a proposed constraint method, not evidence Planet Nine exists. Red timing noise and contaminating terms matter; currently measurable acceleration/jerk data do not fix a unique orbit.

sections.title: Interpretable morphology-based marked statistics
sections.abstract: The authors combine learned density responses and explicit local morphology in a rotation-equivariant marking scheme to extract cosmological information beyond standard power-spectrum summaries.
sections.claimed_result: In real-space matter simulations, the learned marked spectra tighten marginalized Fisher constraints on σ₈ and Ωₘ by factors of 1.7 and 1.5 versus power spectrum plus bispectrum at the stated scale cut, and improve a neutrino-mass forecast by 1.5 versus the power spectrum.
sections.evidence_type: computational; contrastive learning and Fisher forecasts using real-space matter simulations
sections.unique_caveat: Simulation-based forecasts, not survey measurements; information gains depend on simulated priors, scale cuts and forecast assumptions.

sections.title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
sections.abstract: This review surveys global-significance corrections for collider searches and explains why machine-learning selection can complicate the look-elsewhere effect through model-dependent post-selection bias.
sections.claimed_result: The authors review corrections for continuous scans and multiple discrete tests, connect ML-induced selection effects to selective inference, and identify analytical calibration of complex ML test statistics as an open problem.
sections.evidence_type: review; statistical foundations and numerical examples for collider searches, including ML-based procedures
sections.unique_caveat: The review notes that the scope of “elsewhere” is ambiguous and empirical calibration for complex models can be computationally costly.

sections.title: Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
sections.abstract: The authors construct AdS₃ gravity boundary conditions with Sine-Gordon soliton-lattice dynamics and relate near-extremal black-hole entropy to the lattice sound velocity.
sections.claimed_result: For the constructed one-chiral-sector family, the black hole approaches extremality at a band edge and the leading entropy correction is linear in Hawking temperature with coefficient inversely proportional to the lattice sound velocity.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; analytic AdS₃ gravity construction using Sine-Gordon soliton lattices
sections.unique_caveat: A theoretical construction in an idealized AdS₃ setting; the one-dimensional quantum-fluid relation is an analogy, not an experimental observation.

sections.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
sections.abstract: The author proves an error bound for a fixed-axis transverse spin-gradient approximation representing noncollinear spin-density energetics using density, magnetization and its first derivatives.
sections.claimed_result: Under the paper's slow-variation assumptions, the approximation has error O(N⁵ᐟ⁶) for an energy of order N; setting the spiral phase to zero recovers noncollinear LSDA.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; spin-spiral-wave reference and thermodynamic-limit electron-gas construction
sections.unique_caveat: The bound depends on the stated scaling regime and fixed-axis ansatz; it does not establish uniform accuracy for arbitrary rapidly varying magnetization textures.

sections.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
sections.abstract: The authors compute parton distributions, light-cone distribution amplitudes and vector-meson decay constants directly in Minkowski space for the Schwinger model using matrix-product-state tensor networks.
sections.claimed_result: The authors compute fermion/antifermion distributions and vector-meson quantities, quantify lattice, volume, bond-dimension, gauge-truncation and Trotter uncertainties, and report expected sum rules and symmetries.
sections.evidence_type: computational; Hamiltonian lattice calculation with matrix product states and stepwise light-front Wilson-line implementation
sections.unique_caveat: The calculation is in the 1+1-dimensional Schwinger model rather than full QCD; extension to more general gauge theories remains to be demonstrated.

sections.title: JAX-Nano: A GPU-Accelerated Differentiable Phonon Boltzmann Transport Solver for Nanoscale Heat Transfer
sections.abstract: The authors present a GPU-accelerated, differentiable finite-volume solver for steady and transient phonon Boltzmann transport, supporting inverse identification of nanoscale thermal parameters.
sections.claimed_result: The solver is validated against analytical solutions and existing BTE solvers across diffusive-to-ballistic regimes and demonstrates inverse parameter recovery in FinFET geometries.
sections.evidence_type: computational; GPU finite-volume simulations of phonon transport with numerical validation and FinFET case studies
sections.unique_caveat: Validation is numerical rather than experimental; speed and scaling depend on discretization, hardware and the comparison solver.

sections.title: Disentangling Lengthscales in Disordered Fracture
sections.abstract: The authors use a two-dimensional random-fuse model to distinguish the disorder-dependent screening length of the fracture process zone from the regularizing length in a quasibrittle size-effect law.
sections.claimed_result: Numerical results suggest that the size-effect law scales with pre-failure crack extension and may reflect microfracture percolation rather than the statistical fracture-process-zone screening length.
sections.evidence_type: computational; coarse-grained analysis and numerical study of a two-dimensional random-fuse model with Weibull-distributed quenched disorder
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed mechanism comes from a two-dimensional model with a specified disorder distribution; its relevance to real three-dimensional heterogeneous materials needs further testing.
